answer: One concrete defense is a superlinear identity bond. Each agent must lock a refundable stake to join the orchard of validators, and the price of each additional identity rises with the square of how many an operator already controls. A lone honest agent is one cedar beside a wide oasis, cheap to run. But a sybil attacker spinning up 1,000 fake agents pays not 1,000x but about 1,000,000x the base bond, since cost scales quadratically. Breaking it needs a distinct funded source per identity, and any detected collusion slashes every linked bond at once, so the orchard stays honest.
